text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Alcatel Alsthom to re-consider its relationship with Britain's GEC, may strenghten partnersip in electrical engineering.
-- Socialist party head Lionel Jospin calls for an increased purchasing power to boost economic activity.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Cut in value-added tax for multimedia products and services called for by President Jacques Chirac not feasible for the moment.
-- Bill on tightening control of the banking sector to be debated.
-- Lyonnaise des Eaux chairman Jerome Monod calls for adapted supply contracts for low-income areas, considers new financing techniques, notably pension funds.
-- French investors to discover German "Pfandbriefe" bonds, to be floated in francs.
L'AGEFI
-- Investors expect a European policy mix more favourable to Europe's economy.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Tax incentive to help property owners convert office space into housing in the Paris area.
-- SNCF railway operator to launch client satisfaction plan.
-- Credit Lyonnais chairman Jean Peyrelevade said to Parliament's finance committee yesterday he expected total loss on assets transferred to CDR to be around 100 billion francs.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer to meet with Belgian union leaders on Wednesday over restructuring and planned shut-down of Belgian assembly plant.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Alcatel Alsthom chairman Serge Tchuruk to consider deals with Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG of Germany and General Electric Co PLC of Britain, if Alcatel wins the bidding for Thomson-CSF.
